title: add NVTX ranges and microbench instrumentation for runtime profiling
author: Eve Huang
release_notes: Added NVTX annotations and a microbenchmark harness for runtime. Exposes new runtime counters and a Grafana dashboard to track batching/kvcache/kernel latencies. Opt-in via REDWOOD_NVTX=1 or --nvtx flag. No user-facing breaking changes.
body:
Motivation: We need better visibility into per-stage runtime costs (scheduler queueing, kernel launch, KV-cache fetch/hits, and batching) to drive performance tuning and quantify regressions. This PR instruments the runtime with NVTX ranges and lightweight counters, and adds a microbenchmark harness to produce reproducible timing numbers for key code paths.

What I changed: Added an NVTX helper (ScopedNVTXRange) with automatic attribute population, instrumented the serving loop and scheduler entry/exit points, added counters for KV cache hit/miss and batch sizes, exposed aggregated counters on /metrics, and added a small microbench binary and CI smoke job. Also added a Grafana dashboard and a docs page describing how to run traces and interpret NVTX timelines.

Usage: set REDWOOD_NVTX=1 or run the runtime with --nvtx to enable NVTX ranges (no default). Microbench lives under runtime/microbench and can be run with scripts/examples/bench/run_microbench.sh. The microbench outputs JSON summaries that can be uploaded to our perf ingestion pipeline (tools/perf/ingest.py).

Checklist: [x] NVTX utility + RAII wrapper [x] Instrument core runtime hot paths [x] Microbench harness + a few initial cases (single-token loop, kvcache-only, batching-only) [x] Expose counters to /metrics (prometheus format) [x] Grafana dashboard + panels for key metrics [x] Docs and example scripts [x] CI smoke job for microbench (non-flaky)

Notes: NVTX ranges are gated so there is no runtime overhead when disabled. Counters use the existing runtime stats registry to avoid adding a second metrics system. The microbench harness is intentionally small and deterministic to be useful in CI and local debugging.

Commits: See short list below for logical commits included in this PR. Full commit history available in the PR.

Merge: Squash-merged into main after approvals and CI green.

discussion: Michael Torres (reviewer) on 2024-09-13: Nice clean API. One nit: prefer ScopedNVTXRange over NVTXRange to make RAII semantics obvious.
Eve Huang (author) on 2024-09-13: Good point - renamed the class and updated the tests.
Samir Patel (reviewer) on 2024-09-14: Can we gate NVTX behind an env var? NVTX should be opt-in so we don't annotate customer traces by default.
Eve Huang (author) on 2024-09-14: NVTX is gated (REDWOOD_NVTX env var) and additional --nvtx flag added. Updated docs.
Priya Rao (reviewer) on 2024-09-17: Microbench looks useful. Suggest adding a fallback for GPUs without NVTX support to avoid CI flakes.
Eve Huang (author) on 2024-09-17: Added probe for NVTX availability and made microbench skip NVTX annotations when unavailable. Reran CI.
Priya Rao (reviewer) on 2024-09-18: LGTM. Approving for merge.
ci_checks: microbench-smoke: initial-fail (nvtx probe flake) -> rerun -> pass
notes_for_release: Instrumentation and microbench added. Operators can enable NVTX via env var or flags; see docs/perf/instrumentation.md. No API changes. Added Grafana dashboard 'Runtime - NVTX & Microbench' to infra/grafana/dashboards.
how_to_validate: 1) Build runtime with --enable-microbench target; 2) Run examples/bench/run_microbench.sh on a test GPU node; 3) With REDWOOD_NVTX=1 run a few inference requests and capture NVIDIA Nsight Systems timeline to see NVTX ranges; 4) Check /metrics for runtime.kv.hit/runtime.kv.miss and batch size distributions; 5) Open Grafana dashboard 'Runtime - NVTX & Microbench' and verify panels populate.
follow_up: - Add more microbench cases for scheduling heuristics and larger batch sizes (ENG-4602).\n- Integrate microbench runs into nightly perf jobs and auto-upload to perf ingestion pipeline.\n- Consider adding CUPTI counters for deeper GPU kernel metrics in a follow-up PR.
